teaching_context: Related primary-study demonstration, not the older experiment plotted on this slide. Aoki et al. (2022) used a 25-cm running disc and a monitor approximately 5 cm in front of it to measure chicks approaching an artificial imprinting target. Supplementary Video 1 shows the chick running toward that displayed target while the disc returns it to the opposite side. The authors supplied the on-screen stimulus inset and labels; the movie is presented unedited. This demonstrates how an artificial target can elicit approach independently of a live parent.

teaching_context: Related mouse study, not Harlow macaque footage. Movie 4 compares maternal affiliation of postnatal-day-13 mice raised under control conditions (right) or limited bedding (left), tested with an anesthetized dam. The comparison teaches how approach to a caregiver can be measured and how early caregiving history changes proximity seeking. The caregiver here is a living mouse dam, unlike the cloth surrogate in the original slide.
